title: Spec'ing Your Next School Bus: Matching Bus to Route the Right Way
description: Capacity, body style and powertrain are one decision, not three. Here is how the routes you actually run should drive the order sheet.

props.text: Most spec regret traces back to one habit: ordering the bus that replaced the last one instead of the bus the route needs now. Routes change faster than fleets do.
Start with the route, not the capacity

A 77-passenger CE Series and an 84-passenger RE Series are not interchangeable just because the ridership fits. Turning radius, driveway clearance and where the stops sit on a two-lane road decide which one can actually run the route on time.

Count the tightest three turns on the route first. If any of them is a residential cul-de-sac, the conversation is about wheelbase before it is about seats.

IC Bus offers diesel, propane, gasoline and electric across the line. The deciding number is daily mileage against your depot's charging or fuelling reality — an electric CE Series covers a typical Florida elementary route twice over, but only if the depot can put the charge back overnight.

Bring us a week of route sheets and we will spec against them rather than against a brochure.
